name: Viking-Age Ring Fortresses
description: Around 980 CE, Denmark's Viking rulers built five perfectly round earthen fortresses, at Aggersborg, Fyrkat, Nonnebakken, Trelleborg and Borgring. Each has gates facing the four compass points and, inside, longhouses arranged in neat square blocks. Grassy ramparts still trace the circles today, and the forts sit near old land and sea routes, showing how Harald Bluetooth's dynasty projected its power.
